purpose: Measure how fast fast-paced narrated animated shorts change scenes and move, as inspiration for Deep Six cut-paper storybook animation.

method.download: yt-dlp -f 'worst[height>=360]/worst' --download-sections '*0-30' (first 30 s, 360p or lower). On 23 of the YouTube clips ffmpeg got HTTP 403 with the default YouTube client; the same command with the public mweb client (--extractor-args youtube:player_client=mweb) worked each time. No login, no cookies.
method.hard_cuts: ffmpeg -i v.mp4 -vf "select='gt(scene,T)',showinfo" -f null - ; T = 0.30 and 0.20; cut times from pts_time. Average shot length = analysed window / (cuts + 1). Shortest and longest use complete shots only (the last shot is cut off by the window).
method.picture_change: Share of pixels whose colour differs by more than 40/255 between frames 0.5 s (and 1 s) apart, 48 px wide, 10 fps, over the window. Also median frame-to-frame luma change at 10 fps.
method.eyeballed: Scene changes and element beats counted by eye from the 0.5 s contact sheet (first 8 s) and a 0.25 s check sheet. Scene change = clearly new shot, scene or page. Element beat = a new prop, label or paper piece appearing inside a scene.
method.contact_sheets: ffmpeg fps=2, 240 px tall, tile 4x4, first 8 s, timestamps drawn in the corner.

limits: ffmpeg scene detection counts hard cuts only. Zack D. Films, Kurzgesagt and papercraft clips use dissolves, zooms, morphs and camera moves, so the hard-cut counts are far below what the eye sees. Use the eyeballed counts for real scene rate.
Eyeballed counts cover the first 8 s only and are about plus or minus 1.
Only the first 30 s of each video was measured, at 360p. Intros and hooks can differ from the rest.

Audio was not listened to. Narration is confirmed only for the two Zack bug Shorts (YouTube auto-captions, about 3 words per second). For other clips it is inferred from burned-in captions or not assessed.
Views show popularity, not effectiveness. Several papercraft examples are AI-made and have tiny audiences.
Several candidates are 16:9; their pacing transfers, their framing does not.

crawler.note: Steps ceiling is 80 because the API rejects steps above 80 (90 was requested).

videos.title: What Happens To Bugs When You Mow? 😯
videos.creator: Zack D. Films
videos.lead_source: yt-dlp channel Shorts list (@zackdfilms/shorts), keyword scan

ffmpeg_hard_cuts.note: Hard cuts only. Dissolves, zooms, morphs and continuous camera moves are not counted, so cartoon and CG shorts are undercounted.

picture_change.note: Pixels whose colour differs by more than 40/255 between frames 0.5 s or 1 s apart (48 px wide, 10 fps). Counts camera and character motion; does not separate it from cuts.

eyeballed_first_8s.note: Counted by eye from the 0.5 s contact sheet, checked on a 0.25 s sheet. About plus or minus 1.

videos.technique: New macro shot about every 0.6-0.7 s. White 1-3 word captions at the bottom change every 0.6-1 s and each shot shows the thing the words name (mower, blade through grass, mushrooms, insects on soil, cricket eating, caterpillar, ladybug eggs). Camera never rests; changes are camera moves and quick dissolves, so ffmpeg finds almost no hard cuts.
videos.borrow: One new picture for every 1-3 spoken words, held under a second, with the caption naming it.

narration.example: As you begin to mow, you are actually cutting down a forest where thousands of insects are hiding, eating, and laying their eggs.
